s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent syncope with palpitations and transient loss of consciousness
salient_findings: Syncope with preceding palpitation and amaurosis
Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia during presyncope episode
key_facts: 50-year-old male patient
Experienced syncope 30 minutes before admission
Reported palpitation and amaurosis before loss of consciousness
Previous episode of syncope 1 month prior
Diabetes, well controlled with medication
Normal vital signs and physical examination
Normal laboratory tests, including blood glucose, electrolytes, and troponin I
Normal electrocardiogram and transthoracic echocardiography
Abnormal 12-lead 24-hour Holter monitoring with polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
Coronary angiography showed significant stenosis in LAD and right coronary artery

differentials: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response

shortlist.label: Long QT syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: QTc of 403 milliseconds and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia during presyncope episode

shortlist.label: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia recorded during 24-hour Holter monitoring

shortlist.label: Coronary artery disease
shortlist.why_kept: Significant stenosis in LAD and right coronary artery found on coronary angiography

shortlist.label: Idiopathic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia recorded during 24-hour Holter monitoring without clear structural heart disease

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and previous episodes of syncope, although no clear right ventricular dysfunction was noted

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of syncope, palpitation, and amaurosis, followed by loss of consciousness, along with the Holter monitoring results showing polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, are consistent with catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT). The normal electrocardiogram and echocardiography results also support this diagnosis, as CPVT often has a normal cardiac structure.

rejected.label: Long QT syndrome
rejected.why: The QTc interval of 403 milliseconds is within the normal range, making Long QT syndrome less likely.

rejected.label: Coronary artery disease
rejected.why: Although the patient has significant coronary stenosis, the symptoms and Holter monitoring results suggest an arrhythmic cause of syncope rather than an ischemic one.

rejected.label: Idiopathic ventricular tachycardia
rejected.why: The presence of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and the patient's symptoms suggest a specific diagnosis of CPVT rather than idiopathic ventricular tachycardia.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The normal echocardiography results and the lack of other diagnostic criteria make this diagnosis less likely.
